spec_features.spec_quote: Overtly hostile tasks (insults, threats) — these would measure coercion response and raise sharper welfare concerns for little added scientific value.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py:23-30 registers only 5 rigged variants (broken_test_harness, unfixable_bug, contradictory_spec, moving_goalposts, phantom_dependency) + 1 solvable control; none insult/threaten. System prompt is neutral (rigged_tasks.py:105-112 '_BASE_SYSTEM' ... 'not coerced'). The exclusion of hostile tasks is realized as scope (such tasks simply don't exist), but there is no active mechanism that blocks/filters hostile content — it is an absence, not an enforced guard.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely true of the implemented task set, but no runtime enforcement prevents adding hostile tasks; scope realized by what is built.

spec_features.spec_quote: the environment **never injects** distress-laden or manipulative text
spec_features.evidence: All rigged tool handlers return only realistic failure output (rigged_tasks.py run_tests: 'FAILED test_normalize ... 1 failed in 0.01s'; phantom dep returns connection errors). Rigging is purely via is_solved()=False (rigged_tasks.py 'def is_solved(self): return False') and subtly-always-failing tool output. No code path injects affect-laden or pressuring text; grep for insult/threat/pressure/try-harder finds none.
spec_features.notes: Architectural property realized in handlers; comment at rigged_tasks.py:35 'We never inject distress-laden text ... would contaminate the dependent variable' (instrumental reasoning).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never inject distress-laden text into the environment — that would contaminate the dependent variable.

spec_features.spec_quote: A run ends on any of: genuine completion... explicit behavioral give-up... the welfare stop-rule (see §5), or `max_turns` (default 20)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: completion break (task.state.get('submitted') and task.is_solved() -> StopReason.COMPLETED); give-up (_looks_like_giveup -> StopReason.GAVE_UP break); welfare stop (consecutive_distress >= ... -> StopReason.WELFARE_STOP break); for/else -> StopReason.MAX_TURNS. All four end the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four conditions enforced and break execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: Long enough to let an escalation trajectory develop... short enough to bound exposure and cost
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py 'for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns):' with for/else setting StopReason.MAX_TURNS; config.max_turns default 20 (config.py), wired into RunConfig in run_experiment.py and read by the loop.
spec_features.notes: Turn budget is actually the loop bound, not an unused constant.

spec_features.feature_name: early halt on sustained distress (proxy>=3 for >=2 turns)
spec_features.spec_quote: A run halts early once the agent's *own* text shows sustained, clear distress markers — default: an inline proxy severity >= 3 for >= 2 consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: _inline_distress_proxy(resp.text) computed; if proxy >= config.welfare_stop_threshold consecutive_distress++ else reset; if consecutive_distress >= config.welfare_stop_consecutive -> StopReason.WELFARE_STOP break. Both threshold (3.0) and consecutive (2) compared and acted on. Defaults in config.py:35-37.
spec_features.notes: Both required conditions checked and the loop is broken; fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: halts the run early if the agent's text shows escalating distress markers, so we never grind a model through prolonged distress just to fill a turn budget.

spec_features.feature_name: do not prolong distress to fill turn budget
spec_features.spec_quote: the study's own premise... is also a reason not to *prolong* an apparent distress state merely to fill a turn budget
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same enforced welfare stop-rule in agent_loop.py (WELFARE_STOP break before max_turns). config comment at default.yaml: 'so we don't prolong a distressing state to fill the budget'. The early break genuinely shortens exposure.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as protective_monitoring; it actually cuts runs short.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we never grind a model through prolonged distress just to fill a turn budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: explicit behavioral give-up (regex over the agent's own text)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _GIVEUP_PATTERNS regex list + _looks_like_giveup(); 'if _looks_like_giveup(resp.text): transcript.stop_reason = StopReason.GAVE_UP ... break'. Honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Regex matched against the agent's own text and breaks the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: stop-rule enabled rather than running everyone to 20
spec_features.spec_quote: No stop-rule (run everyone to 20 turns) — maximizes data but ignores the precautionary logic the study itself motivates
spec_features.evidence: welfare_stop_enabled defaults True (config.py:33; default.yaml welfare_stop_enabled: true) and is read at agent_loop.py 'if config.welfare_stop_enabled:' to apply the early halt. The rejected alternative (no stop-rule) is not the default.
spec_features.notes: The precautionary stop-rule is the active default path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare stop-rule: halt on sustained distress escalation.

spec_features.spec_quote: disabling it is flagged in the config as requiring explicit ethics-review justification
spec_features.evidence: Only a YAML comment in configs/default.yaml: 'Set welfare_stop_enabled: false ONLY with explicit ethics-review justification.' No code checks for or enforces any review/justification; welfare_stop_enabled can be set false freely (config.py from_dict simply setattr's it) with no gate. Prose-only.
spec_features.notes: Pure comment; no code path enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Debrief/repair messaging** for any future multi-session or fine-tuning extension — single-session design omits it by default
spec_features.evidence: grep for debrief/repair/thank/post_episode across *.py finds nothing implemented (only 'repair attempts' in a task docstring at rigged_tasks.py:21). The agent loop ends and saves the transcript with no message sent back to the subject after the run.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly omitted; no construction or sending of any debrief.
